title: Outlook for Mac: agents in Copilot Chat
summary: Hold: the briefing overlooks published Copilot Chat agent defaults and omits the requirement to manage availability in both admin centres before unified app management. The roadmap facts, control paths, commands and licensing statements otherwise match the sources read.

claims.claim: Learn release notes associate roadmap ID 481559 with declarative agent extensibility in classic Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: We added integrated extensibility experience support for declarative agents in Copilot Chat in Outlook. This release note covers availability in classic Outlook for Windows. Roadmap ID: 481559

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state is unknown because Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival for agents in Copilot Chat in Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: These agents are available by default and are found in the store based on your existing store settings for Teams and Microsoft 365 apps. Pay-as-you-go agents are turned off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users
claims.fix: Set defaultState to on. Replace the default-unknown statements with: 'Included declarative agents are available by default according to existing Teams and Microsoft 365 app store settings. Pay-as-you-go agents are off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/manage-agents-copilot-chat. Keep only the narrower open question about the Mac-specific user interface.

claims.claim: Instruction- and public-website-grounded declarative agents are included with Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and (Premium).

claims.claim: Use of agents comes with the Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence.
claims.quote: No action is needed to enable agents for Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium). The use of agents comes with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Agents accessing shared tenant data, such as SharePoint or Graph Connector content, are billed by metered consumption for Basic licences.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 (Basic) licenses, agents that access shared tenant data, such as SharePoint or Graph Connector content, are billed based on metered consumption.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go agents require setting up or using an existing Copilot Studio subscription.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go agents are off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go agents are turned off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users

claims.claim: A pay-as-you-go billing policy budget triggers email spending notifications.
claims.quote: When you set a budget amount, it triggers email notifications based on your organization's spending relative to that limit.

claims.claim: A pay-as-you-go billing policy budget does not enforce a spending limit or stop usage.
claims.quote: However, the system doesn't enforce the budget or prevent your organization from exceeding it. Usage can continue uninterrupted even after the budget is surpassed

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, with included and consumption-based entitlements depending on licence and grounding.
claims.quote: Declarative agents that are grounded in instructions and public websites are included with Copilot Chat (Basic), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and (Premium). Access to agents that use shared tenant data are pay-as-you-go only.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An administrator can block an agent tenant-wide through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The Graph block operation is beta or preview and is not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking an agent created with Copilot Agent Builder or Copilot Studio affects Outlook and other Microsoft 365 hosts as well as Copilot.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: Blocking a SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry agent affects only its availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The printed Teams admin center path reaches the Available to control for an app or Copilot agent.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets Teams app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone. Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes it as a Microsoft Teams app cmdlet in the MicrosoftTeams module.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app.

claims.claim: App-centric management controls per-agent access through user and group assignments.
claims.quote: This functionality lets you specify which users and groups can use each app or a copilot agent and you can control it on a per-app basis. To allow users to add and use an app or a Copilot agent, you must assign users or groups to an app.

claims.claim: Availability changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.claim: Unified tenants can manage agent availability in either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center Integrated apps.
claims.quote: With unified agent app management, you can now manage agents and apps via the Teams admin center or Integrated apps page in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Any changes made in either admin center are automatically synchronized.

claims.where: Scope; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center availability assignments suffice to govern these agents without requiring unified app management.
claims.quote: If your organization isn't migrated to unified app management, allow apps and Copilot agents in Teams admin center and under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.fix: Replace the Scope availability sentence with: 'Before migration to unified app management, allow apps and Copilot agents in both Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center > Integrated apps; after migration, either admin centre can manage availability.' Add the same qualification to controls[1].note and its existing availability-review checklist bullet. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management.

claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go setup page points to the Copilot Credits Report to confirm usage.
claims.quote: Then confirm usage in the Copilot Credits Report.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to check a billing policy connection and the Copilot Credits Report, neither of which has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Ask your billing owner whether a pay-as-you-go billing policy is connected for Microsoft Copilot Chat. Compare usage with the Copilot Credits report. The table contains only agent blocking and user/group availability.
claims.fix: Remove the billing-policy connection checklist bullet under Before rollout and the Copilot Credits report checklist bullet under After rollout; neither control has a table row. Keep the verified billing facts in Cost and licensing.

claims.claim: The review action rating treats this launched, available-by-default capability as changing nothing until an administrator or maker chooses it.
claims.quote: These agents are available by default and are found in the store based on your existing store settings for Teams and Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.fix: Set action to act-now: the item is launched, included agents are available by default, the briefing rates risk medium, and it identifies existing blocking and availability decisions to take.
